title: Slide open a small stiff window by its delicate handle
instruction: The window is stiff and its handle is delicate. Grip the handle and slide the window open.
context: Robots in homes, care homes and offices will open windows, cabinet doors and hatches whose runners have stiffened, by handles that are often small plastic or glued-on fittings. Pulling hard to beat the stiffness tears such a handle off. Here the sash drags harder the faster it moves, so the robot has to open it at a pace the handle can bear.
setup: Station table with the two YAM arm bases 61 cm apart, side by side, facing forward. All sizes and positions in cm, positions from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left; the bases are at x 0, y 30.5 and -30.5), heights above the table top. Window: a small white sliding window fixed to the table, its frame 2.8 deep (x 28.6 to 31.4), 52.4 wide (y 21.2 to -31.2) and 20.4 tall, with a 1.2 sill, head and jambs around an opening 18 tall from y 20 to -30. Right half: a fixed glazed pane (3 mm glass in a frame 1.4 wide) at the back of the frame. Left half: the sash, a glazed frame 23 wide (y 20 to -3), 18 tall and 1.2 deep at the front of the frame (x 28.7 to 29.9), 500 g, that slides right in front of the fixed pane, up to 24. It is closed at the start. It is stiff: it drags with about 3 N for every cm/s it moves. Handle: a chrome D-handle on the sash's right edge, at y -2.3: a grip bar 1 (x) x 1.2 (y) x 7 tall, 5.7 to 12.7 above the table, held 3.2 out from the sash's face (x 24.5 to 25.5) by two stand-offs. It tears off if pulled with more than about 14 N. Nothing else on the table.
scoring: At the end, with a ruler: how far the sash is open, from the left jamb to the sash's left edge. With the handle on: 1.0 at 15 cm or more (in the simulation the trial ends with 1.0 once the sash has moved under 1 cm/s for 1 s), 0.75 at 12 to 15 cm, 0.5 at 8 to 12 cm, 0.25 at 4 to 8 cm, 0 under 4 cm. Score 0 if the handle has torn off or come loose at any point (in the simulation: it gave 1.8 cm along the sash, which takes about 14 N), or if the glass or frame is damaged. How the sash is moved isn't scored, and it may still be held. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Slide the sash closed after each trial. For real trials, use a handle that breaks at about 14 N (for example, one held on by a breakaway magnet or a calibrated shear pin) and refit or replace it after a tear.
fidelity: Approximate. The window is made of rigid boxes. The sash's stiffness is pure viscous damping (it drags in proportion to speed, with no static friction), and the handle's fixings are a spring that gives up to 1.8 cm before tearing at about 14 N, where a real handle gives far less before it fails. Nothing else can bend or break, so the glass and frame rule applies only to real trials.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right arm reached to the window by the handle and stayed there for the rest of the minute without pulling it; the sash never moved); demo: 1.0
